title: Basic 2 · Shift an image
summary: Same one-node cycle as rotate, applied to a translation (dx, dy) with the Shift node.

steps.title: Try translation
steps.body: Shifting an image right/left, up/down is called translation. It's the workhorse of particle centring in cryo-EM.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Clock face** onto the canvas.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The `data.clock` node now shows its image so you can see the starting input.

steps.title: Drop the Shift node
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Shift** onto the canvas.

steps.title: Wire Clock → Shift
steps.body: Drag from Clock's `image` output to Shift's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With defaults (dx = dy = 0), Shift is a pass-through, so the output matches Clock exactly — a baseline before you set a shift.

steps.title: Click Shift
steps.body: Click Shift. The Inspector reveals `dx` (horizontal, + = right), `dy` (vertical, + = down), `cval` (the fill value for freshly-exposed border pixels), and `interpolation`.

steps.title: Set dx to 30
steps.body: Enter **30** in `dx`. The image slides 30 pixels to the right.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. The clock shifts 30 pixels right; the 30 freshly-exposed pixels on the left are filled with `cval` (0 = black).

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: Set `dy` too for a diagonal shift. Non-integer values (e.g. 1.5) force interpolation, so changing `interpolation` changes the result (see Comparison 1). Next, **Basic 3 · Pad an image** introduces the Pad node for resizing.
